chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ismail ibn Yasar, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Israil, from Yunus, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Harith Al-Awr, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not carry the females upon the saddles, lest you incite them to immorality.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْفُرُوج: Females / Women (plural of farj, referring to the private part or the woman herself)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on carrying women on saddles in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam Ali (AS) offers a nuanced view on gender segregation, linking the physical posture of riding in a saddle—typically associated with male authority and exposure—to the psychological state of 'tahyij' (incitement or arousal). Shia scholars interpret this not merely as a prohibition of transport, but as a preventive measure against fitnah, emphasizing that modesty (haya) extends to the preservation of sexual purity through controlled public visibility. This reflects the broader jurisprudential principle of maintaining social boundaries to safeguard moral integrity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ismail Bin Yasaar, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Israil, from Yunus, from Abu Is’haq, from Al Haris Al Awr who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not carry the female upon the saddle, for they would be incited for the immorality’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ’Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Ishaq from al-Harith al-‘A’war who has said the following: “
’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must not allow female organs to ride on saddle to excite them for indecent and sinful acts.’”
